cite.quote: 1. Initial This is the starting state and indicates that HSRP is not running. This state is entered via a configuration change or when an interface first comes up.

2. Learn The router has not determined the virtual IP address, and not yet seen an authenticated Hello message from the active router. In this state the router is still waiting to hear from the active router.
3. Listen The router knows the virtual IP address, but is neither the active router nor the standby router. It listens for Hello messages from those routers.

4. Speak The router sends periodic Hello messages and is actively participating in the election of the active and/or standby router. A router cannot enter Speak state unless it has the virtual IP address.

5. Standby The router is a candidate to become the next active router and sends periodic Hello messages. Excluding transient conditions, there MUST be at most one router in the group in Standby state.

6. Active The router is currently forwarding packets that are sent to the group's virtual MAC address. The router sends periodic Hello messages. Excluding transient conditions, there MUST be at most one router in Active state in the group.

intro.quote: Coup messages are sent when a router wishes to become the active router.

steps.explain: B sends a Hello message with its current state, Hellotime, and Holdtime.

cite.quote: The router sends a Hello message with its current State, Hellotime and Holdtime.

steps.explain: B sends a Coup message to tell the active router that a higher-priority router is available.

cite.quote: The router sends a Coup message to inform the active router that there is a higher priority router available.

steps.explain: A sends a Resign message so another router can become the active router.

cite.quote: The router sends a Resign message to allow another router to become the active router.

intro.quote: The format of the data portion of the UDP datagram is:

fields.name: Version
fields.explain: Identifies the HSRP message version; this RFC describes version 0.

cite.quote: Version: 1 octet The version of the HSRP messages. This document describes version 0.

fields.name: Op Code
fields.explain: Identifies the message type. The defined types are Hello, Coup, and Resign.

cite.quote: Op Code: 1 octet The Op Code describes the type of message contained in this packet. Possible values are: 0 - Hello 1 - Coup 2 - Resign

fields.name: State
fields.explain: Carries the sending router's current state in the HSRP state machine.

cite.quote: State: 1 octet Internally, each router in the standby group implements a state machine. The State field describes the current state of the router sending the message.

fields.name: Hellotime
fields.explain: Gives the approximate interval between the router's Hello messages, in seconds.

cite.quote: Hellotime: 1 octet This field is only meaningful in Hello messages. It contains the approximate period between the Hello messages that the router sends. The time is given in seconds.

fields.name: Holdtime
fields.explain: Gives how long the current Hello message should remain valid, in seconds.

cite.quote: Holdtime: 1 octet This field is only meaningful in Hello messages. It contains the amount of time that the current Hello message should be considered valid. The time is given in seconds.

fields.name: Priority
fields.explain: A higher value wins the election; if priorities tie, the router with the higher IP address wins.

cite.quote: Priority: 1 octet This field is used to elect the active and standby routers. When comparing priorities of two different routers, the router with the numerically higher priority wins. In the case of routers with equal priority the router with the higher IP address wins.

fields.name: Group
fields.explain: Identifies the standby group to which the message belongs.

cite.quote: Group: 1 octet This field identifies the standby group. For Token Ring, values between 0 and 2 inclusive are valid. For other media values between 0 and 255 inclusive are valid.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: Reserved octet in the HSRP packet format.

cite.quote: Reserved

fields.name: Authentication Data
fields.explain: Contains the clear-text eight-character reused password.

cite.quote: Authentication Data: 8 octets This field contains a clear-text 8 character reused password.

fields.name: Virtual IP Address
fields.explain: Carries the virtual IP address used by the standby group.

cite.quote: Virtual IP Address: 4 octets The virtual IP address used by this group.
